subject: Re: Unit economics deep dive — pricing & token volumes
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Parker <john.parker@fintechx.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: unit economics questions / next steps

John — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned:  

Summary of what you shared
- Current: pilot using contextual search + summarization for support triage (~2M tokens/month today).
- Target: ramp to 50–100M tokens/month within 6–9 months if latency & cost look good.
- Key metrics you care about: target cost per $/1M tokens (budget range $500–$1,200/1M), $/feature (API call feature-level cost target ~$0.02), and CAC payback window (target 6–9 months).

Open questions we’ll validate
- Exact token mix (prompt vs generation vs embeddings) — you said ~60% embeddings, 30% generation, 10% system prompts; please confirm in the attached spreadsheet.
- Whether you need Private/Dedicated (for compliance) vs Hosted — you mentioned procurement would prefer hosted if unit costs are consistent.

Preliminary economics (back-of-envelope)
- Hosted list pricing (no commitment): ~ $1,000 / 1M tokens for generative-eq models; embeddings priced separately.
- Committed pricing (annual or 12-mo reserved): we can get to ~$650–$800 / 1M tokens depending on volume and SLA.
- For 50M tokens/mo at $700/1M -> ~$35k/mo. If 50% of tokens are embeddings with lower unit cost, effective blended $/1M may be ~ $550.
- $/feature estimate: with 3k tokens per feature on average, at $700/1M this is ~$2.10 per 1k tokens -> ~$6.30 per feature — but this depends heavily on average tokens/feature (we should validate).

Next steps
1) John: confirm the "Monthly_Volume" tab in the attached spreadsheet (FinTechX_Monthly_Volume_Estimates.xlsx) with exact split (embeddings vs gen).
2) Redwood: Naomi + Aditya will run a unit-economics model (blended $/1M, $/feature, CAC payback sensitivity) and share a short deck.
3) Schedule 30-min technical deep-dive with our solutions engineer to validate latency and dedicated vs hosted trade-offs (suggest Tue/Wed next week).

Attachments: FinTechX_Monthly_Volume_Estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the model and a proposed meeting time once Naomi confirms the assumptions.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182
From: John Parker <john.parker@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Li <sasha.li@fintechx.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: unit economics questions / next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. I attached the preliminary volume sheet we use internally (see Monthly_Volume tab) — numbers are rough but directionally right. A few clarifications:  

- The 60% embeddings / 30% generation / 10% prompts split is our current expectation but could shift to 50/40/10 as we add more retrieval.
- Our procurement team gave a budget range of $20k–$40k/month for year one tooling (we may frontload more spend if performance is strong).
- CAC target: we’re modeling payback at ~8 months on LTV assumptions; so we need predictable per-user inference cost to model margin.

Can you provide a quick estimate for 100M tokens/month (hosted list vs committed)? Also, please highlight any assumptions about tokenization differences between models — we’re comparing a few model variants on the call.

Attachment: FinTechX_Monthly_Volume_Estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet)

—John
John Parker | Head of ML Platforms, FinTechX
john.parker@fintechx.com | +1 212-555-0100
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: unit economics questions / next steps (internal)

Looping in for the unit-econ calc — will run three scenarios (Pilot: 5–10M/mo, Mid: 50M/mo, High: 100M/mo).
Planned deliverables:  
- Blended $/1M tokens (hosted list vs committed discount tiers)
- $/feature (assuming 2.5k / 3k / 4k tokens per feature sensitivity)
- CAC payback sensitivity (6 / 8 / 12 month windows) and margin impact (gross margin vs inference spend)
- Recommendation: whether Dedicated makes sense for unit cost or only for compliance at these volumes

Assumptions I’ll use (will call out in the deck): list gen $1,000/1M, list embeddings $400/1M; committed discounts 25–40% depending on term & volume. If you have alternative model-specific unit costs (e.g., LlamaX vs Redwood-curated gen variants), drop those here.

I’ll aim to have a 1-pager + a spreadsheet by tomorrow EOD PT.

—Naomi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Parker <john.parker@fintechx.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: unit economics questions / next steps

John — thanks for the file and the procurement context. Quick answers + a conservative pricing example to help procurement model:  

Conservative hosted list (no commitment) estimates
- Generation: $1,000 / 1M tokens
- Embeddings: ~$400 / 1M vectors-equivalent
- Blended for their 60/30/10 split: approx $760 / 1M tokens

Committed (12-mo reserved) illustrative pricing
- 10–50M / mo: $700 / 1M (blended)
- 50–100M / mo: $550 / 1M (blended, higher commit)
- 100M+ / mo: $425–$500 / 1M with an annual contract and predictable usage patterns

Examples (blended):
- 50M/mo at $700/1M -> $35k/mo (expected gross margin impact: inference spend ~X% of ARR contribution depending on feature monetization)
- 100M/mo at $550/1M -> $55k/mo

$/feature back-of-envelope (assume ~3k tokens/feature average)
- At $700/1M -> 3k tokens = 0.003 * $700 = $2.10 per feature call
- At $550/1M -> ~$1.65 per feature call

CAC payback illustrative (using your 8-month target)
- If average contribution margin per customer is $1,200/mo and inference adds $200/mo, incremental payback changes by ~1–1.5 months. We’ll show row-level math in the one-pager.

Dedicated vs Hosted note
- Dedicated can lower unit inference costs at very high sustained utilization (100M+/mo) due to fixed-cost amortization and higher discounts on kernels/quantization. For the 50–100M band, committed hosted pricing + batching/caching optimizations often closes most of the gap while keeping ops simpler. We’ll include a build vs buy sketch.

Next: Naomi will share the 1-pager/spreadsheet today. Can we book the solutions deep-dive Wed 14:00 PT? That gives us time to validate tokenization math and model selection trade-offs before procurement pushes formal RFx.

—Marissa
From: John Parker <john.parker@fintechx.com>

Thanks — that all helps a lot. Wed 14:00 PT works for the deep-dive. Quick ask before then: can you include a 100M/mo worked example (hosted list vs committed vs ballpark dedicated cost) in the 1-pager so procurement can see the delta? Also confirm whether the committed tiers require an annual minimum.

I’ll bring Sasha from procurement to the deep-dive. Looking forward to the numbers.

—John
